Criteria of Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium in Transient Plasmas

Source: R/lte_criteria.R
lte_criteria.Rd

Checks the local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) of a laser-induced plasma by the McWhirter criterion and by the temporal and spatial criteria of Cristoforetti et al. (2010) for transient and inhomogeneous plasmas.

Usage

lte_criteria(
  temperature,
  electron_density,
  delta_e,
  oscillator_strength,
  mass,
  gaunt = 0.2,
  time = NULL,
  length_scale = NULL,
  tolerance = 0.1
)

Arguments

temperature

The plasma temperature, in K.

electron_density

The electron density, in cm\(^{-3}\).

delta_e

The energy gap of the transition, in eV.

oscillator_strength

The absorption oscillator strength of the transition.

mass

The atomic mass of the species, in u, or its element symbol (such as "Ca").

gaunt

The effective Gaunt factor. Default is 0.2.

time

Optional times of the measurements (one per temperature), in s, for the temporal criterion.

length_scale

Optional length over which the temperature and density change, in mm, for the spatial criterion.

tolerance

The largest relative change (or ratio of lengths) for a criterion to be satisfied. Default is 0.1.

Value

A tibble with one row per measurement (the arguments are recycled to a common length): the temperature, electron_density and delta_e; the McWhirter minimum_density and whether it is reached (mcwhirter); the relaxation_time (s) and diffusion_length (mm); with time, the time, the relative changes of the temperature and of the density during the relaxation time (temperature_change, density_change) and whether the temporal criterion is satisfied; with length_scale, the length_ratio of the diffusion length to it and whether the spatial criterion is satisfied.

Details

The McWhirter criterion (see mcwhirter_criterion()) gives the minimum electron density for collisions to dominate the population of the levels in a stationary, homogeneous plasma. It is necessary but not sufficient in a laser-induced plasma, whose temperature and density change in time and in space (Cristoforetti et al., 2010):

  • Temporal criterion: the plasma must change little during the time \(\tau_{rel}\) it takes to relax to equilibrium, \(|T(t + \tau_{rel}) - T(t)| / T(t) \ll 1\), and likewise for \(N_e\), with $$\tau_{rel} \approx \frac{6.3 \times 10^4}{N_e f \langle g \rangle} \Delta E\, (k_B T)^{1/2} \exp\left(\frac{\Delta E}{k_B T}\right)\ \mathrm{s}$$

  • Spatial criterion: the temperature and density must change little over the distance \(\lambda\) an atom diffuses during \(\tau_{rel}\), $$\lambda \approx \frac{1.4 \times 10^{12}}{N_e} (k_B T)^{3/4} \left(\frac{\Delta E}{M f \langle g \rangle}\right)^{1/2} \exp\left(\frac{\Delta E}{2 k_B T}\right)\ \mathrm{cm}$$ which must be much shorter than the length over which they change, such as the size of the plasma.

Here \(N_e\) is in cm\(^{-3}\), \(\Delta E\) and \(k_B T\) in eV, \(f\) is the absorption oscillator strength of the transition across the gap \(\Delta E\), \(M\) the atomic mass of the species (u) and \(\langle g \rangle\) the effective Gaunt factor (Van Regemorter, 1962). The slowest transition to equilibrate is usually the resonance transition between the ground state and the first excited level of the species, such as Ca II 393.37 nm (\(\Delta E\) = 3.15 eV, \(f\) = 0.68); nist_lines() gives the oscillator strengths (fik). The effective Gaunt factor depends on the transition and on \(\Delta E / k_B T\); the default, 0.2, errs toward long relaxation times. The criteria are order-of-magnitude checks.

The temporal criterion needs the temperature and density at several times, time (such as acquisition delays): their relative changes during \(\tau_{rel}\) are computed from their rates of change between the measurements (finite differences of their logarithms). The spatial criterion needs the length over which they change, length_scale. A criterion is satisfied when the relative change, or the ratio of the diffusion length to length_scale, is at most tolerance.

References

  • Cristoforetti, G., De Giacomo, A., Dell'Aglio, M., Legnaioli, S., Tognoni, E., Palleschi, V., Omenetto, N. (2010). Local thermodynamic equilibrium in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy: beyond the McWhirter criterion. Spectrochimica Acta Part B, 65(1):86-95.

  • Van Regemorter, H. (1962). Rate of collisional excitation in stellar atmospheres. The Astrophysical Journal, 136:906-915.

See also

mcwhirter_criterion(), boltzmann(), electron_density()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

# Ca II resonance transition (393.37 nm), in a plasma of 1 mm
lte_criteria(temperature = 9000, electron_density = 1e17, delta_e = 3.15,
             oscillator_strength = 0.68, mass = "Ca", length_scale = 1)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   temperature electron_density delta_e minimum_density mcwhirter relaxation_time
#>         <dbl>            <dbl>   <dbl>           <dbl> <lgl>               <dbl>
#> 1        9000             1e17    3.15         4.74e15 TRUE             7.46e-10
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: diffusion_length <dbl>, length_ratio <dbl>, spatial <lgl>

# a plasma cooling from 1 to 5 microseconds
lte_criteria(temperature = c(11000, 9500, 8500, 7800),
             electron_density = c(3e17, 1.5e17, 8e16, 5e16), delta_e = 3.15,
             oscillator_strength = 0.68, mass = "Ca", time = c(1, 2, 3, 5) * 1e-6)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 11
#>   temperature electron_density delta_e minimum_density mcwhirter relaxation_time
#>         <dbl>            <dbl>   <dbl>           <dbl> <lgl>               <dbl>
#> 1       11000           3  e17    3.15         5.25e15 TRUE             1.31e-10
#> 2        9500           1.5e17    3.15         4.87e15 TRUE             4.13e-10
#> 3        8500           8  e16    3.15         4.61e15 TRUE             1.15e- 9
#> 4        7800           5  e16    3.15         4.42e15 TRUE             2.60e- 9
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: diffusion_length <dbl>, time <dbl>,
#> #   temperature_change <dbl>, density_change <dbl>, temporal <lgl>
